newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo platinum, palladium futures end higher.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo platinum, palladium futures end higher.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo platinum and palladium futures ended higher, due to uncertainty over Russian exports and short-covering by local investors, traders said.
Platinum futures were five to 35 yen higher, with benchmark June ending up 11 yen at 1,356 yen per gram.
Russia's platinum group metal (PGM) export agency Almazjuvelirexport informed Japanese buyers that it would resume platinum exports next week, traders said.
"Russia's palladium exports have resumed, but exports of platinum haven't," a trading house official said. "We're still worried about whether they will actually deliver platinum."
The six-month suspension of Russian PGM exports, caused by bureaucratic problems there, sent world palladium and platinum prices soaring and caused an acute supply tightness.
Palladium futures ended sharply higher. The August and October contracts rose by their daily 22 yen limit-up by the close, and benchmark June closed 14 yen up at 536 yen per gram.
"Some players actively covered their short positions, because Russia recently resumed palladium shipments," another trade house official said.
Japanese traders said that Tokyo PGM futures were expected to remain volatile until next week.
Tokyo gold futures ended six to 12 yen higher, with benchmark June 1998 up nine yen at 1,176 yen per gram.
Bullion was quoted at $318.60/319.00 per ounce at 0755 GMT, lower compared to Wednesday afternoon New York levels.

News earlier on Thursday that Australian Prime Minister would inquire into WMC Ltd chief Hugh Morgan's involvement in the Reserve Bank of Australia's decision to sell most of its gold reserves had little impact on the Tokyo gold futures, traders said.
Benchmark June silver futures was down 1.9 yen at 159.5 yen per 10 grams. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk (+81-3-3432-7391)
